pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks all existing rows are 0 and the CHECK constraint.
test 'AC-2' checks / and ?view=open list only open items in id order.
test 'AC-3' marks 3 and 1 done and checks the ✓ prefix and id order.
test 'AC-4' checks the order, ✓ on done items and no mark on open ones.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav markup for each view and for /.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.

test 'AC-7' and the states tests cover all three messages. The test is real evidence. However a late commit rewrote the item to 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a real step (see the high finding).
traffic/routes.json lists both routes. test 'AC-8' checks them.

findings.what: Commit f6b81c9 ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) edited AC-7 after the owner's go (2026-10-12). It appended 'verified by review: checked by hand' to the item. There is no decision in the spec recording an owner call or date. 'Checked by hand' is also not a followable step. The edit reworded an acceptance item and turned a test-proven item into a review-proven one.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit edited AC-7 after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or state the change in the PR with the owner's decision.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. The default view is open and the view is a query parameter. It adds no write route or cookie.
All 6 state-table rows have tests. The late commit f6b81c9 edited AC-7 without a recorded decision.

The tests assert behaviour (parsed list items and messages). The only change to an existing test is the fake app in test/traffic.test.js now recording the query string, and that does not loosen it. I did not run the test suite here, because CI runs it.
README describes the views. Nothing stale that I found.
src/index.js: Object.hasOwn guards the view value, the SQL fragments are constants, and the empty-table fallback is correct.
The view value is allowlisted and titles are HTML-escaped. No injection path found.
The diff adds no stylesheet or templates beyond minimal inline HTML in src/index.js, so there is no UI design to review.
There are no UI screenshots or a browser flow. The HTML is checked by tests.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see the finding). The title is under 72 characters.
